params.why: C must be a whole number

stem: Solve the quadratic equation in the set of complex numbers, giving the roots in terms of $i$ with any square root simplified: ${=a}x^2+{=B1}x+{=C1}={=e}x+{=f}$
solution: Collect all terms on the left: ${=a}x^2+{=B}x+{=C}=0$, so $a={=a}$, $b={=B}$, $c={=C}$.
notes: Advanced: rearrange to standard form, then formula with negative discriminant whose root needs simplifying (e.g. sqrt(-12)=2i sqrt3). Discriminant is -s^2 n with n squarefree, so every instance is complex non-real. Roots are not reduced further; any equivalent form is accepted by value marker.
